images.text:
Dear readers,

This week I have blogged about environmental issues. I don't consider myself to be much of an environmentalist, but if nobody acts now, what will become of our planet? If I had been more aware of these issues when I was young, I would have littered less and paid more attention to green issues. This week, I interviewed eco-experts and took questions from concerned citizens. Here are the main topics that are being discussed these days:

1. Contamination from oil spills and dumping of garbage - these issues have slowly come to the forefront of people's minds.
  2. The hole in the ozone layer is being widened by deforestation and the buildup of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
  3. Public awareness has been raised by programs like “adopt-a-whale” and recycling initiatives. More materials would be recycled and repurposed if people were given more access to information.

What is being done in your area to help the environment? What eco-efforts have been implemented in your country? Do you think they will ultimately make a difference? I am waiting to hear your ideas and whether you think we can truly make a difference for future generations.
Write back soon green warriors!

The Passive: The Present Continuous and Present Perfect Tenses

You use the Present Continuous to talk about an action that is happening at the time of speaking. The action or event is in progress.
I am waiting to hear your ideas and whether you think we can truly make a difference.

You use the Present Perfect to talk about a finished action or event with present consequences. There is a connection between what happened in the past and the present.
These issues have slowly come to the forefront of people's minds.

You often choose the passive form when you want to talk about an action but are not so interested in saying who or what does/did it. Passives without agents (the doers) are common in academic and scientific writing.

There are four types of conditional sentences in English:
  1. Zero Conditional - to talk about certainty and facts
  2. First Conditional - to talk about real possibilities in the present or the future
  3. Second Conditional - to talk about unreal possibilities in the present or the future
  4. Third Conditional - to talk about unreal past situations
You use third conditional to talk about unreal situations in the past. These are things that did not happen in the past. You often use the third conditional to talk about regrets.
